The project aims to establish India’s first underwater museum, artificial reef and submarine tourism destination Listen to this article : The project draws inspiration from international wreck-diving destinations such as the USS Oriskany in Florida. Pic/ Special Arrangement Maharashtra’s marine tourism sector has received national recognition, with the Maharashtra Tourism Development Corporation’s (MTDC) INS Guldar project in Sindhudurg district winning the prestigious The Week Heritage Award - Golden Banyan Award 2026. Tourism Minister Shambhuraj Desai described the honour as a matter of pride for the state. The project aims to establish India’s first underwater museum, artificial reef and submarine tourism destination. articles.title: IIT Hyderabad Director B S Murty urges youth to help build a developed India - Telangana Today
articles.content: NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | Hyderabad | Iit Hyderabad Director B S Murty Urges Youth To Help Build A Developed India IIT Hyderabad Director B S Murty urges youth to help build a developed India IIT Hyderabad Director Prof. B S Murty addressed a Distinguished Lecture Series at the University of Hyderabad, urging young people to drive national development through science and technology. He highlighted self-reliance, global manufacturing ambitions and sustainability initiatives at IIT Hyderabad By Telangana Today Published Date - 28 October 2026, 04:01 PM Hyderabad : As part of the ongoing Golden Jubilee celebrations of the University of Hyderabad (UoH) and the Silver Jubilee celebrations of its School of Management Studies, the campus hosted a Distinguished Lecture Series featuring Prof. B S Murty, Director of IIT Hyderabad, who delivered a talk on the theme ‘Building a Developed India: Role of Education’. Emphasising the importance of national development, Prof. Murty said that true progress went beyond self-reliance. “We have to make ‘Make in India’ products—not just to be self-reliant, but to supply globally so we may call India a developed nation,” he asserted. He challenged the youth to take the country’s destiny into their hands over the next 20 years, urging accelerated development in science and technology. Citing examples from IIT Hyderabad, he said the institution had banned single-use plastics and transformed barren lands into lush green spaces, demonstrating how young minds could drive significant change. “Only Indian-born individuals care for India the most, and our youth should be fearless in their pursuits,” he said. articles.title: Sarvam to build AI applications for Indian military - TechGig
articles.content: Homegrown AI startup Sarvam has signed a five-year memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) and the Ministry of Defence. Under this agreement, Sarvam will develop and deploy AI technology for the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force. The MoU establishes an umbrella framework for AI projects across the three Services and joint organisations under HQ IDS. Sarvam will create AI applications for operational, training, and decision-support requirements, also providing technical support. This agreement aligns with the government's push for Atmanirbharta , or self-reliance, in defence and the indigenisation of defence equipment and capabilities. AI for national security The work under the MoU will be undertaken by Chanakya , Sarvam's firewalled division focused on national security and defence. Chanakya will use Sarvam's AI stack, including foundation models such as Sarvam 105B . Sarvam and HQ IDS will also work on projects of critical importance, including an AI fabric connecting elements of India 's defence capabilities. The agreement focuses on using AI in multiple areas, including decision support , target acquisition, and data fusion across the sensor-to-shooter loop. Human oversight will be retained over operational decisions. The proposed AI layer will be built in India using Indian data and computing infrastructure and deployed on sovereign infrastructure. The Indian armed services will gain access to common foundation models, agentic infrastructure, and geospatial and perception systems, allowing doctrine and lessons learnt to inform subsequent work across the Services. "Sarvam exists to build AI in India, for India," Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar said. "The core of that mission is to put the country’s own intelligence into the systems it depends on."
